synopsis_paragraphs: Theatre of Darkness: Yamishibai 17 (Yami Shibai 17 / 闇芝居 十七期) episode 12 sits in late-cour pressure, when habits are no longer enough. This is not a plot dump. The public catalog pitch is only a floor: Seventeenth season of Yami Shibai. What the week actually asks is whether ILCA used that floor as architecture or as wallpaper.

Genres on the tin read Horror, Supernatural; the useful question is which of those labels got camera time and which were merchandising. Community score currently hovers around an unranked haze, which tells you heat, not craft. We read the episode as a turning-point document: who gained a new obligation, who lost a convenient lie, and whether the cour’s theme got more expensive. Theatre of Darkness: Yamishibai 17 is being watched as a live product of original adaptation. Japanese viewers argue about pacing against the source and about whether new episodes add a relationship change or only another demonstration of power. If you only remember a super move, you watched the trailer inside the episode. If you remember a silence, a blocked doorway, or a joke that hurt, you watched the show. Radar note unique to episode 12: this week we grade the episode as a close-up problem: who is allowed to occupy the frame without a power effect, and whether ILCA trusts a face longer than a title card. Japanese same-night talk usually splits into people who wanted a trailer and people who wanted a scene. We side with the scene. If you are reading this briefing instead of a wiki recap, that is the contract.

Our desk treats those tells as primary sources of reception, not as a substitute for watching. When they explode, isolate whether the praise is for a single hero cut or for sequence direction. Only the latter predicts a good cour.
